t: G'day, and welcome to Japaneiji — episode one. This is your personal Japanese podcast, built entirely from the words in your own vocab list — plus a handful of trip essentials you'll want this week in Japan.

Here's how it works. I'll introduce words in English, you'll hear the Japanese twice — say it out loud in the gap, don't just think it. And every few minutes there's a listening check: you'll hear a full Japanese sentence, twice, with a pause to work out the meaning before I reveal it. No notes needed — this is for the car.
Good morning — polite, for the chalet breakfast room.
Now, meeting people. When you join that chalet group in person, here are the two bonus essentials.
Nice to meet you — literally, it's the first time.
Please be good to me — the untranslatable friendship handshake. Together they make the full self-introduction.
よろしく おねがいします
よろしく おねがいします
はじめまして。よろしく おねがいします。
First listening check. Someone greets you in the morning and comments on the day. What are they saying?
おはようございます。きょうは さむい です。
おはようございます。きょうは さむい です。
It means: Good morning. Today is cold.
おはようございます。きょうは さむい です。
Section two. The politeness pack — the four words that do eighty percent of tourist Japan. Most of these aren't in your quiz list yet, so listen hard.
Thank you — the full polite version.
ありがとうございます
ありがとうございます
Excuse me, sorry, and also: waiter! The single most useful word in Japan.
Please give me — stick it after anything you want.
Pattern time. Sumimasen gets attention, kudasai gets things. Listen.
すみません。ひるごはん を ください。
Excuse me — lunch, please. Try the pattern with anything.
Listening check. You're at the till. What does the shopkeeper want to tell you?
さんぜん えん です。
Three more from your sound-change set — the six-hundreds and the eight-thousands.
Six thousand — and notice: this one has no sound change at all. Roku-sen, single S.
Eight thousand — hachi squeezes to a small tsu, but the S stays an S.
ろっぴゃく えん です。
はっせん えん です。
さんぜん えん です。
It means: It's three thousand yen — en is the Japanese word for yen, no Y sound.
さんぜん えん です。
Section three — and this one matters, because you're driving. Japanese road signs.
Stop — on the red triangle. The one sign you must know.
Exit — you'll hunt this word on every expressway and car park.
Car park full — man means full.
Spaces available — kuu means empty. Same sha, opposite fortunes.
Free — you don't. Mu means nothing.
Quick contrast drill. Listen to the pair.
Paid. Free. If you only remember mu — nothing — you'll never pay the wrong one.
Listening check. You pull up to a car park and the sign talks to you. What's the bad news?
この ちゅうしゃじょうは まんしゃ です。
この ちゅうしゃじょうは まんしゃ です。
It means: This car park is full.
この ちゅうしゃじょうは まんしゃ です。
East — Tokyo is the eastern capital.
And your bonus power question: doko desu ka — where is it. Attach it to anything.
えきは どこですか。
Where's the station? Now with a place you already know.
ちゅうしゃじょうは どこですか。
Listening check. You ask a local for the station and get this. Which way, and is it far?
えきは ひだり です。ちかい です。
えきは ひだり です。ちかい です。
It means: The station is to the left. It's near.
えきは ひだり です。ちかい です。
Section five. Money. You already drilled the tricky sound-change numbers — here they are earning their keep.
Fee or toll — you'll see it at every tollgate.
Three hundred — san plus hyaku, the H softens to B.
Eight hundred — hachi squeezes to a small tsu, H becomes P.
Three thousand — the S voices to Z.
Now hear them as prices. En — yen — goes on the end.
さんびゃく えん です。
はっぴゃく えん です。
さんぜん えん です。
Listening check. The tollgate machine speaks. What's the toll?
りょうきんは はっぴゃく えん です。
りょうきんは はっぴゃく えん です。
It means: The fee is eight hundred yen.
りょうきんは はっぴゃく えん です。
Quick shopping interlude — the pointing words. In a Japanese shop you barely need nouns; you need these three.
Add kudasai and you can buy anything in the country.
これ を ください。
This one, please. Now the price check pattern, both directions.
それは いくらですか。
How much is that one? And a warning word — takai. In your list it's tall or high, but about prices it means expensive.
あれは たかい です！
That one over there is pricey!
Listening check. You point at something, the shopkeeper answers. What are you being told?
これは ろっぴゃく えん です。
これは ろっぴゃく えん です。
It means: this one is six hundred yen.
これは ろっぴゃく えん です。
Section six. You're going to the snow — so, weather.
Snow — the whole reason for the trip.
Cold — the air, the weather, the day.
Cold to the touch — the snowball, the beer, your hands.
That pair is a classic trap, so hear them side by side.
きょうは さむい です。
Today is cold — the air. And.
ゆきは つめたい です。
The snow is cold to touch. Samui for weather, tsumetai for things.
Listening check. Morning at the chalet, someone gives you the forecast. What's coming?
きょうは くもり です。あしたは ゆき です。
きょうは くもり です。あしたは ゆき です。
It means: Today is cloudy. Tomorrow — snow.
きょうは くもり です。あしたは ゆき です。
Particle reminder: o marks the thing the verb happens to. Listen to the shape.
あさごはん を たべます。
I eat breakfast. Same shape, different pair.
おちゃ を のみます。
I drink tea — ocha, green tea, a bonus word you'll hear constantly.
While we're here — a sixty-second tense tour, using eat. Present.
Past negative — I didn't eat. The big mouthful.
Hear all four in a row, and feel the endings do the work.
たべます。たべません。たべました。たべませんでした。
Same machine runs every polite verb you own — drink, watch, listen, go.
Listening check. Your chalet mate announces a plan. What is it?
ひるごはん を たべます か。
ひるごはん を たべます か。
It means: Shall we eat lunch? — the ka on the end turns it into a question.
ひるごはん を たべます か。
One more quick kit before the survival section — time. Lift passes, checkout, dinner bookings: everything in Japan runs on the clock.
Put it together — asking the time.
いま なんじ です か。
What time is it now? And an answer.
いま じゅうじ です。
Listening check — a plan for tomorrow. When and what?
あした、さんじに いきます。
あした、さんじに いきます。
It means: tomorrow, we go at three o'clock — the ni after sanji marks the time.
あした、さんじに いきます。
Section eight. The survival kit — the honest words for when it all goes sideways.
I don't understand — say it early, say it proudly.
It's OK, I'm fine, no worries — the great Japanese all-clear.
The polite word for it — honourable hand-washing place.
Look out! Dangerous — shouted on ski slopes.
Danger — the word on warning signs.
Hot spring — your reward after the slopes.
The emergency sentence, all pieces you now own.
すみません。わかりません。
Excuse me — I don't understand. Follow it with daijoubu and a smile, and Japan will forgive you anything.
Final section check. You're lost in the town. Ask where the toilet is — then hear the answer.
おてあらいは どこですか。みぎ です。ちかい です。
おてあらいは どこですか。みぎ です。ちかい です。
It means: Where's the restroom? It's to the right — close by.
おてあらいは どこですか。みぎ です。ちかい です。
Now — the chalet scene. A thirty-second dialogue using only what you've learned today. First, straight through — just let it wash over you.
おはようございます。きょうは さむい です ね。
まあ、ふゆ です。あしたは ゆき です か。
はい。だいじょうぶ です。
あさごはん を たべます か。
もちろん。おちゃ を のみます。
Second pass — line by line. Repeat each one out loud in the gap. Shadowing like this is the fastest way to make it stick.
きょうは さむい です ね。
Ne on the end is the friendly — isn't it.
あしたは ゆき です か。
はい。だいじょうぶ です。
あさごはん を たべます か。
もちろん。おちゃ を のみます。
That whole conversation — greeting, weather, snow forecast, breakfast, and heading out — is one hundred percent your vocab list. That's the point of all this.
Now we flip the direction — the production round. This is the real skill: I give you English, you say the Japanese out loud before the answer comes. Ten of them.
ありがとうございます
ありがとうございます
Say: stop — the road sign word.
Say: it's cold today — the weather kind of cold.
きょうは さむい です
きょうは さむい です
Ask: where is the toilet? Polite version.
おてあらいは どこですか
おてあらいは どこですか
How many did you get out before me? That number is your real speaking score.
Last section — the review round. Eight sentences, everything mixed. Each plays twice, then a pause. Translate out loud before I do. Score yourself out of eight.
こんにちわ。はじめまして。
こんにちわ。はじめまして。
この こうそくどうろは ゆうりょう です。
この こうそくどうろは ゆうりょう です。
This expressway is a toll road.
でぐちは みぎ です。
でぐちは みぎ です。
The exit is on the right.
りょうきんは さんびゃく えん です。
りょうきんは さんびゃく えん です。
The fee is three hundred yen.
あしたは はれ です。
あしたは はれ です。
ゆきは つめたい です！
ゆきは つめたい です！
すみません。えきは どこですか。
すみません。えきは どこですか。
わかりました か。だいじょうぶ です。
わかりました か。だいじょうぶ です。
Did you get it? — It's all OK.
Before we close — the driving signs one last time, rapid fire. Picture each sign as you hear it.

And that's episode one. If you scored five or more out of eight, you're travel-ready. The bonus words today — arigatou gozaimasu, sumimasen, kudasai, ikura desu ka, en, ocha, and doko desu ka — aren't in your quiz yet; ask me and I'll add them. Safe driving, enjoy the snow — and remember: samui is the weather, tsumetai is the snowball. Mata ne!
ありがとうございました。またね！
